title: Optionals and async Swift
summary: Return an optional safely, then diagnose a forced unwrap in a lookup.

scenario.briefing: A campus app looks up the first positive reading and may find nothing. Represent absence without crashing.

misconceptions.description: Force unwrapping a lookup that may fail.
misconceptions.feedback: first returns an optional. Handle nil explicitly instead of forcing it.

misconceptions.description: Blocking a thread to wait for async work.
misconceptions.feedback: Use await. Blocking defeats the concurrency model and can deadlock.

sections.title: Swift functions and collections
sections.body: Functions declare parameter and return types: func add(_ left: Int, _ right: Int) -> Int { left + right }. Array<Int> or [Int] stores an ordered collection, and Dictionary stores key-value pairs. Async functions and actors structure concurrent work.

sections.title: Swift errors and tools
sections.body: A throwing function uses throws, and callers use do/catch or try?. Optionals are not errors; they represent a legitimate absence. Swift Package Manager resolves dependencies, swift build compiles, swift test runs tests, and Xcode provides the IDE.
